assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single nucleic-acid molecules electrically as they thread a nanopore rests on a clear physical principle (ionic-current blockade) and delivered a genuinely new capability: portable, long-read, label-free sequencing, plus a platform for single-molecule chemistry. It sits exactly where physics, chemistry and biology meet and has opened broad, unforeseen applications.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brenner and Deamer showed polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin; Deamer and Branton conceived sequencing by this route; Bayley engineered pores and adapters; Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled ratcheting that made base reading practical. Three is a defensible set, but the original idea (Deamer, Branton) versus engineering (Bayley) versus the working ratchet (Akeson) is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Commercially validated for over a decade and independently confirmed worldwide; recognition is timely, with accuracy still improving but the principle long settled.
uncertainties: Whether Daniel Branton, Hagan Bayley or others are still living is uncertain to me and would constrain the configuration.
Credit between the original concept and the enzyme-ratchet engineering is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving the bond-level chemical structure of individual molecules with CO-functionalised noncontact AFM is conceptually elegant and quantitative, approaches atomic resolution of chemical bonds, and enabled direct observation of on-surface reactions and unknown products. A physicist would regard the principle as clear and the result as iconic.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor and high-resolution frequency-modulation AFM; Gross, Meyer and colleagues at IBM Zurich demonstrated the chemical-structure imaging with functionalised tips. Eigler and Ho contributed earlier single-atom manipulation and STM spectroscopy, which is arguably a different discovery; separating them gives a clean three-person set.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories since 2009; mature, though use in routine chemistry is still niche.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or physics, given the instrumentation basis.
Overlap with the STM prize (1986) and with Eigler and Ho's atom-manipulation work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single nucleotides in living cells without double-strand breaks, a new chemistry-driven capability that follows directly from the 2020 CRISPR recognition and has direct therapeutic consequences. The concept was original and the generative potential is very large.
assessment.attribution: David Liu is the decisive originator and leader, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainee authors of the cytosine and adenine editors. A single-laureate prize is plausible, though crediting the junior authors is not standard and Kondo and Nishida's parallel Target-AID work could be raised.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use has begun and many groups have independently confirmed it; the field is still young and clinical outcomes are early, so timing is on the early side but defensible.
uncertainties: Prize overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may feel incremental to some members.
Parallel Target-AID work by Nishida and Kondo complicates priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity degradation reframes small-molecule drug action: a bifunctional molecule or molecular glue recruits an E3 ligase to destroy a target. It opens previously undruggable targets and is supported by a growing clinical pipeline, giving clear generative potential.
assessment.attribution: Crews (with Sakamoto and Deshaies) introduced PROTACs; Ciulli provided VHL ligands and mechanistic structures; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining glue degraders. The configuration is a compound discovery with several defensible subsets, and Deshaies, Sakamoto, Ito and Gray are all arguable.
assessment.maturity: Multiple degraders are in late-stage clinical trials but no approvals of PROTACs yet to my knowledge, so maturity is partly forward looking.
uncertainties: Compound discovery whose PROTAC and molecular-glue parts may need different recognition.
I am not certain of the current clinical status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and ionic motion in a single Lagrangian scheme, a clear principle that made ab initio simulation of liquids, interfaces and reactions routine. Its originality, transparent two-person attribution and decades of impact are strong.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is the unambiguous origin and the credit is clean; no third name is needed.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of independent use and extension make this fully mature; if anything the concern is that it is long overdue and that Chemistry has already honoured computational methods in 1998 and 2013.
uncertainties: Whether the committee feels computational chemistry is sufficiently recognised after 2013.
Parrinello also appears in metadynamics and machine-learned potentials candidates, which could dilute or reinforce his case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based computational design, linking adsorption energies to catalytic activity through scaling relations and the d-band picture, converted catalysis into a predictive quantitative science with real catalysts discovered in advance. The principle is fundamental and fits a physicist's preference for a simple underlying law.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the clear intellectual leader; Hammer (not in the list) co-developed the d-band model, and Rossmeisl, Mavrikakis, Jaramillo and Scheffler contributed variously, so a clean three-person split is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Predictions have been repeatedly validated experimentally (e.g. hydrogen evolution, ammonia, methanol), though the field remains evolving with machine learning.
uncertainties: Credit to Hammer and others outside the credited names cannot be addressed.
Strength of experimental validation across the whole framework versus selected showcases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a physical-chemistry idea with enormous generative potential for cell biology, disease and drug discovery. A physicist finds the thermodynamic framing compelling.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed P granules behave as liquids (2009); Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction phase transitions with defined proteins in 2012. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory and sequence grammar, so the set is contested.
assessment.maturity: The principle is widely adopted but debate continues about physiological relevance and over-use of the label; a prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Ongoing controversy over in vivo relevance and the quantitative rigor of many claims.
Whether the discovery is chemistry or cell biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators on clustered arrays made genome-scale sequencing cheap and routine, an unmistakably transformative capability across biology and medicine. The chemistry of the reversible-terminator method is central.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa method; others (Ju, Mayer, Rothberg) developed rival or related chemistries, so attribution is complicated and the commercial path blurs the scientific credit.
assessment.maturity: Technology is fully mature and ubiquitous; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Competing parallel technologies (pyrosequencing, Lynx, Ju's terminators) make priority hard to separate.
Sanger and Gilbert already honoured sequencing in 1980, which may affect appetite.
